newsitem.title: UK: Turkish bank Yapi sets debut Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: Turkish bank Yapi sets debut Eurobond.

text.p: Turkey's largest private bank Yapi Kredi launched its first Eurobond on Wednesday, offering investors a sizeable yield pick-up over U.S. Treasury notes to compensate for event risk, bankers said.
The $150 million five-year was priced to yield 395 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, with an appealing 10.0 percent coupon.
"It offers excellent value and we expect the spread to tighten," the UBS syndicate manager said.
Bankers away from the lead said it was a well-priced bond and would attract retail investors.
"It looks cheap for the name," a banker said.
The mandate was awarded in March this year.
Following investor presentations there had been firm interest in the bond from private banks in Europe, from British funds, from Asia as well as some offshore U.S. interest, UBS said.
Earlier this year, Standard & Poor's downgraded Yapi Kredi and six other Turkish banks to speculative grade, citing the burden of Turkey's rising budget deficit on the banking system.

Economy minister Gunes Taner said recently he expected year-on-year inflation to reach around 100 percent by the end of 1997 compared to a forecast of 85 percent made earlier by the three-week-old coalition government.
Dealers said the yield allowed for this risk.
"There is always event risk in a country like Turkey," a dealer said.

UBS said Yapi's bond issue was intended to cover its demand for medium term financing, primarily corporate lending, without incurring significant maturity mismatches. Turkey's five-year dollar bond, which was increased to $400 million in May, trades at around 275 bp over U.S. Treasury notes versus a launch spread of 350 b.p, dealers said. The paper pays a 10.0 percent coupon.
Turkey is rated B1 by Moody's and B by S&P.
A number of Turkish banks have tapped the mark sector including Emlak, Halkbank and Ottoman bank, due to the large customer base in Germany.
"This is a good introduction to the dollar sector for other Turkish banks," UBS said. Yapi is owned and controlled by the Cukurova group, the third largest conglomerate in Turkey.
